title: Analyzing Hippocampal Neural Stem Cell Quiescence from Single-Cell RNA Sequencing Data
author: Hart, Harris
materials: high-performance computer with 32 GB of RAM and 4 CPUs

1.Perform the analysis in R, ideally using RStudio, on Linux, macOS, or Windows operating systems.
Note: We recommend a system with at least 32 GB of RAM and 4 CPU cores. On a high-performance computing cluster, request equivalent resources.

2.Install the key software packages listed in the key resources table. For example: > install.packages("Seurat") Note: Although using different software versions (e.g., Seurat) and computational environments will alter data visualization, the fundamental analytical approaches remain stable. The goal of this protocols paper is to demonstrate the key principles we have employed to isolate hippocampal NSCs from scRNA-seq data. Therefore, when implementing this protocol, especially for different datasets, follow the biologically-informed guidance and alter code accordingly (e.g., the clusters to isolate).
Insufficient cluster resolution used to identify cell populations.
Inability to distinguish proliferating NSCs from IPCs.
Clear batch or replicate effects in sequencing data.

steps.title: Prepare hardware environment
steps.instruction: Perform the analysis in R (preferably via RStudio) on Linux, macOS, or Windows. Use a system with at least 32 GB RAM and 4 CPU cores (or request equivalent resources on a computing cluster).

steps.title: Install required software
steps.instruction: Install the key software packages listed in the key resources table, e.g., run `install.packages("Seurat")` in R.

steps.title: Set up RStudio project and data
steps.instruction: Launch RStudio, create a new project named **Mycn_NSC_analysis**, install the packages from the key resources table, download the count matrices from GEO accession **GSE280296** (samples GSM8594261, GSM8594263, GSM8594260, GSM8594262), create a folder called **data** inside the project directory, and move the downloaded matrices into that folder.

steps.title: Read and merge scRNA‑seq samples
steps.instruction: Read the four scRNA‑seq samples and merge them into a single Seurat object.

substeps.instruction: Open the script `01_read_merge.R` in the tutorials folder.
Run the code in that script; it reads the four Mycn datasets, merges them, performs QC filtering, and adds metadata (batch and genotype).

steps.title: Normalize and integrate by batch
steps.instruction: Normalize and integrate the four experimental samples according to experimental replicate (batch) using SCTransform.

substeps.instruction: Open the script `02_normalise_integrate_neurogenic.R` in the tutorials folder.
Run the code; it performs batch‑corrected integration on all cells, then visualizes marker genes to isolate neurogenic lineage clusters.

steps.title: Isolate neurogenic clusters
steps.instruction: Identify and subset the three neurogenic clusters (quiescent NSCs, proliferating NSCs/IPCs, immature neurons).

substeps.instruction: Define key genes for visualization: `ngenic_ident <- c("Hopx", "S100b", "Eomes", "Dcx")`.
Normalize RNA assay: `final.integrated <- NormalizeData(final.integrated, assay = "RNA")`; set default assay to RNA.

Generate feature plots for each key gene with `FeaturePlot(object = final.integrated, features = ngenic_ident, reduction = "umap", dims = c(2,1), pt.size = 1)` and save as `Figure_1B.png` (dpi 300, height 7 in, width 10 in).
Create a UMAP cluster label plot with `DimPlot(final.integrated, label = TRUE, reduction = "umap", dims = c(2,1), pt.size = 1)`. Combine side‑by‑side with the feature plots for visual comparison.
Subset the object to retain only clusters 0, 1, and 7: `final.integrated <- subset(final.integrated, idents = c("0", "1", "7"))`.

steps.title: Renormalize neurogenic cells
steps.instruction: Renormalize and integrate the four experimental samples now containing only neurogenic lineage cells.

substeps.instruction: Open the script `03_normalise_integrate_neuralstemcells.R` in the tutorials folder.
Run the code; it performs a second round of batch‑corrected integration, removes contaminating clusters, and isolates NSCs by selecting cells with high Hopx or high Apoe expression.

steps.title: Isolate neural stem cells (NSCs)
steps.instruction: Identify NSCs and separate proliferating NSCs from IPCs using marker visualization.

substeps.instruction: Set default assay to RNA: `DefaultAssay(final.integrated) <- "RNA"`.
Generate a full UMAP plot: `DimPlot(final.integrated, label = TRUE, reduction = "umap", pt.size = 1) + NoLegend()`.
Create FeaturePlots for Apoe, Hopx, Eomes, Dcx, and S100b with appropriate `max.cutoff` values (Apoe = 3, Hopx = 3, Eomes = 1, Dcx = 1, S100b = 1) and `pt.size = 1`.
Crop each plot to coordinates `xlim(-6, 0.8)` and `ylim(-9, 4)` for focused views.
Arrange full and cropped plots side‑by‑side using the pipe syntax shown, and save as `Figure_2.png` (dpi 300, height 8 in, width 20 in).
Visually inspect Hopx/Apoe‑high inner ring (proliferating NSCs) versus Eomes‑high outer ring (IPCs) and select NSCs accordingly (high Hopx or high Apoe).

steps.title: Renormalize NSC population
steps.instruction: Renormalize and integrate the four samples now containing only quiescent and proliferating NSCs.

substeps.instruction: Open the script `04_normalise_integrate_quiescentneuralstemcells.R` in the tutorials folder.
Run the code; it performs a third integration round on the NSC population and prepares for removal of proliferating NSCs.

steps.title: Isolate quiescent NSCs
steps.instruction: Exclude proliferating NSCs and other contaminating clusters to retain only quiescent NSCs.

substeps.instruction: Generate a DimPlot of the current object: `p1 <- DimPlot(final.integrated)`.

Interactively select cells to remove (e.g., contaminating neuroblast cluster) with `cells_to_remove <- CellSelector(p1)` and subtract them: `final.integrated <- subset(final.integrated, cells = setdiff(Cells(final.integrated), cells_to_remove))`.
Visualize proliferation markers with `FeaturePlot(final.integrated, features = c("Mki67", "Mcm2", "Pcna"), ncol = 3)`.
Remove the proliferating cluster (cluster 5) using `final.integrated <- subset(final.integrated, idents = "5", invert = TRUE)`.

Create a final UMAP of the cleaned quiescent NSC set: `p3 <- DimPlot(final.integrated, reduction = "umap", group.by = "seurat_clusters", label = FALSE, pt.size = 1) + ggtitle("UMAP of Clusters")` and optionally combine with earlier plots for comparison.

steps.title: Statistical comparison of pseudotime
steps.instruction: Perform a Kolmogorov‑Smirnov test to compare pseudotime distributions between conditions (e.g., Mycn control vs cKO). Choose alternative statistical tests if distributional assumptions are violated.
